title: [Export] fields/properties broken when originating from a secondary csproj.
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: 4.7.2-stable-mono

### System information

Godot v4.7.2.stable.mono (ed1daf0bf) - Arch Linux #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Fri, 28 Aug 2026 16:09:39 +0000 on Wayland - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 (nvidia; 610.57.04) - AMD Ryzen 9 5950X 16-Core Processor (32 threads) - 31.23 GiB memory - Dummy (44100 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

I am attempting to do a multiplayer game, and thought it best to split the project into client/shared/server project files, with shared containing a package reference to `GodotSharp` and `Godot.SourceGenerators` so that I can reuse node code for server and client.
The issue I am having though is that nodes defined in my `ScopeCreeps.Shared` project, be it instantiated directly or inherited by another node in `ScopeCreeps.Client`/`ScopeCreeps.Server`, have issues with fields/properties marked as `[Export]` in the class.
Such members are unable to have their values tweaked in the inspector window and seem to always result in the default value. This is a problem especially when needing a reference to another node, the value ending up being null/undefined.
Note that I mean the default value for the type, not the default value specified when defining the member. For example, if you do:
```cs
[Export] public float TestFloat = 35.53f;
```
and you log the value of `TestFloat` on `_Ready()`, it will print `0`.

### Steps to reproduce

- Create a new project, make a directory to house it such that the project is contained in a subdirectory (e.g. `Project/Project`).
- Set solution directory to the parent directory (`../`).
- Generate the C# solution.
- Open an IDE and create a second C# project, make sure it is not in the same directory as the `project.godot` file. Should look like the following:
```
- Root Directory
  - Project
    - project.godot
    - Project.csproj
  - SubProject
    - SubProject.csproj
  - Project.sln
```
- Edit the subproject `.csproj` to include the following packages:
```csproj
<ItemGroup>
    <PackageReference Include="Godot.SourceGenerators" Version="4.7.2" />
    <PackageReference Include="GodotSharp" Version="4.7.2" />
</ItemGroup>
```
- Create a node script in the subproject, give it an `[Export]` member. Something along the lines of this:
```cs
using Godot;
namespace Subproject;

public partial class TestNodeSubProject : Node
{
    [Export] public bool TestBoolSubProject;
}
```
- Include the subproject in the main project's `.csproj`:
```csproj
<ItemGroup>
    <ProjectReference Include="..\SubProject\SubProject.csproj" />
</ItemGroup>
```
- Create a node script in the main project. Inherit the node from the subproject. Inheriting is not required but it lets you see both members in the same inspector window. It should also have an `[Export]` member:
```cs
using Godot;
using Subproject;
namespace Project;

public partial class TestNodeProject : TestNodeSubProject
{
    [Export] public bool TestBoolProject;
}
```
- In the editor, create any scene to load into, and attach the `TestNodeProject` script or whatever you called it to that root node.
- Attempt to alter the members in the inspector window

You will be able to freely toggle `TestBoolProject` but any attempts to alter `TestBoolSubProject` will fail. The output console will spit out a message saying you've set the value but the value will remain the default.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[MultiProjectMRP.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32154992/MultiProjectMRP.zip)
Contains the following:
```
- MultiProjectMRP
  - MultiProjectMRP
    - .editorconfig
    - icon.svg
    - icon.svg.import
    - MultiProjectMRP.csproj
    - node.tscn
    - project.godot
    - TestNodeProject.cs
    - TestNodeProject.cs.uid
  - SubProject
    - SubProject.csproj
    - TestNodeSubProject.cs
  - MultiProjectMRP.sln
```
